fit_reason: Makes DRAM, NAND and NOR memory and is one of the three major DRAM suppliers, with HBM and server memory sold into data centers. Memory is the whole business, so it sits at the center of the tight DRAM, HBM and flash supply.
One of the world's largest memory makers, selling DRAM and NAND. It is widely recognized as the HBM leader, and memory is its entire business.

Designs and makes NAND flash storage (SSDs, embedded memory, wafers). NAND is the tier that gains as context moves down the memory tiers, and suppliers have added little NAND capacity. Flash is its whole business.
Makes flash-based SSDs and memory wafers for data centers alongside a large hard disk drive business. Flash is a meaningful part of the company, but HDDs are still a large share.
Designs memory subsystems for servers and HPC, including DDR4 DIMMs, NVDIMMs and storage-class memory. Memory modules are all it does, but it is a small player.

Its Integrated Memory segment supplies DRAM modules, SSDs and flash for AI and networking customers. Memory is one of three segments next to AI and HPC computing and LEDs, so it is a meaningful part, not the core.
Supplies DDR5 and DDR4 memory interface chips to module makers, plus memory interface IP. It benefits from server memory volume, but it does not make the memory itself.

Designs NAND flash controllers for SSDs, including enterprise and data center drives, and sells to the major NAND makers. Its volume follows NAND demand, but it is a controller supplier, not a memory maker.
Makes probe cards that test DRAM and NAND/NOR chips, a core use for the product. More memory capacity means more probe card demand, though it supplies none of the scarce memory.
Leading maker of etch and deposition equipment, including through-silicon via etch used in HBM stacking. Memory fabs are a large customer group, but the company also serves logic.
Largest supplier of wafer fabrication equipment, selling to both memory and logic makers. Memory capacity additions raise demand for its tools, but memory is only part of the business.
Makes thermo-compression and flip-chip advanced packaging equipment, which matters for stacking memory dies in HBM. Memory is one of several end markets for its assembly tools.
Leading supplier of semiconductor test systems, including systems for memory devices. Memory test is a meaningful but not the main part of a business tilted to SoC and AI accelerator test.
Semiconductor test maker whose Magnum platform tests flash and DRAM. Memory test is one product line within a larger business that also covers SoC, robotics and wireless test.
Makes inspection and metrology tools for advanced packaging and memory components, which includes HBM-related inspection. Memory is one of several customer areas.
Makes dicing saws, grinders and polishers for thinning and cutting wafers, which are used in stacking memory dies. Its exposure to memory is indirect and the description is thin.

Sole supplier of EUV lithography and a leader in DUV, with systems used to make DRAM and NAND as well as logic. Memory capacity additions raise lithography demand, but memory is only part of its sales.
Leader in wafer inspection and process control tools used by memory and logic fabs. Memory capacity additions raise demand for these tools, but memory is only part of the business.
Supplies specialty chemicals, filtration and wafer-handling materials to logic and memory chip makers. Its exposure to memory is through volume, and memory is named as a customer group.
Makes deposition, etch and annealing equipment, and its description names DRAM among the devices its tools are used for. Memory is one end use among several, including photonics and power devices.
Makes metrology systems for process control in chip fabs, with memory producers named as customers. Memory is one of several customer groups alongside logic and foundry.
Makes inspection, metrology and packaging lithography tools used in advanced packaging, which includes memory stacking. Memory is not named as a core focus.
Makes ion implantation machines for chip fabs. Memory capacity additions raise demand for equipment, but the description does not tie it to memory specifically.
Makes single-wafer wet cleaning systems used in advanced-node and 3D patterned wafer fabrication, including memory. Memory exposure is inferred, not stated in the description.
Makes burn-in and test systems for logic, optical and memory chips, including wafer-level burn-in. Memory is one of several device types, so exposure is partial.
Supplies vacuum, power delivery and process control components for etch and deposition tools in chip fabs. It benefits from added memory fab capacity, but only indirectly and among many markets.
Makes gas delivery and fluid subsystems for semiconductor capital equipment makers. Its demand tracks equipment volume, so memory capacity additions help only indirectly.
Makes gas and chemical delivery subsystems for semiconductor capital equipment. Its demand tracks equipment volume, so memory capacity additions help only indirectly.
Supplies electronic materials for making semiconductor chips. The description is thin and does not say how much is memory, so it is kept as borderline.
Makes connectivity chips for AI infrastructure, including memory connectivity products such as CXL. Memory connectivity is one part of a platform built mostly around data and network links.
Provides outsourced semiconductor packaging and test, including stacked memory packages and NAND/SSD modules. Memory is one of many end markets and the description does not mention HBM.
Sells high-speed DRAM modules for PCs, alongside gaming peripherals and PC components. DRAM modules are a small part of a consumer hardware business.
Sells flash-based data storage systems for enterprise customers. It is a buyer of flash rather than a maker, and the description is thin.
